blocks.markdown: Some Croatian verbs always appear with the small reflexive particle **se**, which — unlike Italian or French reflexive pronouns — never changes for person or number: **zvati se** (to be called), **igrati se** (to play), **radovati se** (to look forward to / be happy about).

Like other clitics, **se** follows the second-position rule: it sits right after the first stressed word or the verb, not necessarily at the end. **Djeca se igraju** (The children are playing) — *se* comes right after the subject *djeca*.

exercises.prompt: Kako ___ zoveš? (se — What's your name? — informal)
Which particle never changes form, regardless of the subject?
Translate: "The children are playing." (igrati se — se follows the subject)
